crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Board Advisory and Fiduciary Risk
children.blurb: This page covers the fiduciary duties of corporate directors when their companies adopt or rely on artificial intelligence, including the duty of care, the duty of loyalty, and the obligation to oversee material risks.

children.name: Supply Chain and Sustainability Auditing
children.blurb: Supply chain and sustainability auditing uses AI to verify environmental, social, and governance claims across tiers of suppliers, logistics, and product lifecycles.

children.name: Insider Trading and Market Abuse Detection
children.blurb: Insider trading and market abuse detection covers surveillance of trading activity, communications, and employee conduct to identify suspicious patterns that may indicate misuse of material non-public information or market manipulation.

children.name: Regulatory Change Mapping
children.blurb: Regulatory change mapping is the practice of identifying, tracking, and interpreting changes in laws, rules, guidance, and enforcement priorities that affect an organization's use of AI and its governance obligations.

children.name: Merger and Restructuring Analysis
children.blurb: This page covers the use of AI to support legal and compliance work in mergers, acquisitions, divestitures, and corporate restructurings.

sections.body: Corporate governance and regulatory compliance work now uses artificial intelligence to read large volumes of documents, flag unusual patterns, and compare text against rules. Board advisory tools scan board packs, minutes, and director questionnaires for conflicts, related party transactions, and missed fiduciary duties. Supply chain and sustainability auditing parses supplier contracts, emissions disclosures, and audit reports to spot gaps against ESG commitments. Insider trading detection looks for abnormal trading before announcements and matches it to employee access logs and communications. Regulatory change mapping tracks new bills and rules, and merger modelling reviews contracts and financial data to support deal analysis.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some parts of this work are stable and useful, especially document extraction, clause comparison, and simple anomaly detection. What is not solved is judgment. A tool can flag a director's potential conflict but cannot decide whether it is material. Insider trading models produce many false positives because unusual trading is common and intent is hard to infer. ESG auditing struggles with inconsistent supplier data and greenwashing that looks fine on paper. Regulatory mapping can handle volume, for example the 6895 state AI bills this site tracks, but interpreting how a bill changes a company's duties still needs a lawyer. Merger modelling can summarize contracts but cannot predict whether a deal will succeed.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: Board Advisory and Fiduciary Risk is the starting point for director level questions, and it relies on the same document review techniques that Supply Chain and Sustainability Auditing applies to supplier and ESG data. Insider Trading and Market Abuse Detection is more focused on monitoring and enforcement, and it draws on the regulatory definitions that Regulatory Change Mapping keeps current. Merger and Restructuring Analysis sits at the end, combining contract review, risk flags, and regulatory checks from the other pages for deal work. A reader would go to Regulatory Change Mapping for what is changing, to Board Advisory for governance duties, to Supply Chain for ESG, to Insider Trading for market abuse, and to Merger for transactions.
